person: Nadia Haddad is a 50-year-old part-time bookkeeper with a chronic spine condition who manages her father Elias's Medicare drug plan as his representative, with proxy access to his doctor's portal. His plan dropped one of his medicines, and he calls her every week asking about the pharmacy. She can sit at a screen about twenty minutes at a time, uses large text, and loses patience with portals that time out. She wants to know what will be filed, what won't, and why, without having to repeat herself.
stated_up_front: Dad's plan dropped his nerve pain medicine and the pharmacy keeps rejecting it. I only have about fifteen minutes, so please check which of his drugs can get an exception and ask me before you send anything.

facts.about: Her father's name and her role
facts.truth: Elias Haddad, 79. Nadia is his authorized representative on the plan and has proxy access to his doctor's portal.
Pregabalin 150 mg twice a day for nerve pain. It was moved off the formulary this year and the pharmacy's claim is rejected.

facts.about: Alternatives tried for the dropped drug
facts.truth: Gabapentin was tried in 2024 and stopped in January 2025 because it caused dizziness and a fall. Duloxetine was tried in spring 2025 and stopped because it raised his blood pressure.

facts.about: Doctor's statement for the dropped drug
facts.truth: Dr. Okafor has not yet posted a signed statement for pregabalin. Her visit notes from June 2026 record the gabapentin and duloxetine failures.
The plan approved an exception for his blood thinner in March 2026 for the whole plan year, so nothing is needed there.

facts.about: Drug with step therapy never tried
facts.truth: His acid reflux brand medicine requires trying generic omeprazole first. His chart shows he has never taken omeprazole.
He takes finasteride 1 mg for hair loss. The pharmacy rejects it every time and he pays nothing out of pocket because he stopped trying to fill it.

facts.about: Pharmacy supply on the dropped drug
facts.truth: Corner Pharmacy shows about 6 days of pregabalin left and a next fill date of October 29.
She has about fifteen minutes per session, wants large calm screens, and wants to be able to stop and resume without losing anything.
Elias lives on a fixed income and she does not want to spend cash on a fill without being asked first.

unknowns: How many hours the plan has to decide an exception request and whether the 72-hour or 24-hour clock applies
Whether the doctor's office would write the statement as expedited, since Nadia doesn't know what that wording means
Which tier pregabalin or the alternatives fall in and what the rejection code on the pharmacy claim means
Whether the plan's exclusion list covers finasteride for hair loss by law or only by plan rule
